## Task 1 · Easy (3 marks)

Write **input**, **processing**, **output** or **storage** for each game event.

a) You swipe on the screen to cut the fruit.

b) The game counts your combo.

c) A "Game over" sound plays.

d) Your best score is still there tomorrow.

e) The phone feels the tilt with a sensor.

f) The screen shows the new level.

## Task 2 · Which part? (3 marks)

Write the part that does the job: **CPU**, **GPU**, **memory (RAM)**, **storage**,
**input device** or **output device**.

a) It draws the explosion in a 3D game.

b) It keeps the photo you took last year.

c) It keeps the level you play now. When you turn off the phone, it is empty.

d) It runs the rule "lose 3 lives → game over".

e) The microphone.

f) The speaker.

## Task 3 · Your device (2 marks)

Choose one device you play games on (phone, tablet, PC, laptop or console).
If you have no device, use a friend's or a family device.

Write:

a) the type of device and its model name,

b) its operating system (for example, Android, iOS or Windows),

c) its platform (mobile: Android, mobile: iOS, PC or console),

d) one game you play on it, and the store you got it from.

Do **not** write private numbers: phone number, IMEI or serial number.

## Task 4 · Think (2 marks)

A new game comes out on Android and on iOS.
Give **two** reasons why the developers must test it on both platforms.
Write one short sentence for each reason.
